To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a general Ginzburg-Lanau theory for superconducting QCD and applied it to a vortex in quark matter.
we have developed a new method for studying the magnetic and gluon-magnetic properties of quark matter in the color superconductivity state.
we have investigated the magnetic properties of color-flavor locked superconducting quarks in the presence of rotated electromagnetism, which is an effect of the Higgs mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of superconducting color quark matter in compact stars.
the investigation of the properties of quark matter in the presence of strong magnetic fields in the framework of Ginzburg-Lau-dae theory.
the magnetic properties of color-superconducting quark stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Ginzburg- Landau description of superconducting quarks in a neutron star is a viable approach, and it can be used to study the magnetic properties of quark matter in a neutron star.
the color superconductivity of quark matter leads to an electric Meissner effect and a color Meissner effect.
the color superconductivity of quark matter leads to a Higgs mechanism and to a Meissner effect in quark matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the color superconductivity of quark matter leads to the occurence of Meissner currents for both the electric as well as the color magnetic field.
the color superconductivity is a necessary condition for the occurence of Meissner effects in quark matter.
